S17.title: Reporting, reproducibility, and methodological-transparency summary for the revised primary analysis.
rows: Eligibility required an ICU length of stay of at least 48 hours. The prediction landmark was the end of the first 48 hours after ICU admission; operationally, the estimand was the probability of a later-documented HAP/VAP event after the landmark and before ICU exit.

The observation window varies with remaining ICU stay and is not a fixed 7-day or 14-day incidence probability. Standardized exact infection-onset, ICU-exit, and death times were not retained, so fixed-horizon or competing-risk redefinition was not reliable; incipient infection at the landmark cannot be excluded.

Two attending neurologists independently reviewed clinical progress notes, chest radiographs/CT, temperature, WBC, sputum or respiratory-secretions, oxygenation, and intubation/MV timing. The pneumonia index time was the earliest documented concurrence of a new/progressive radiographic infiltrate and compatible clinical infection evidence. Reviewers were blinded to model outputs; disagreements were resolved by a third senior neurologist (chief physician).

Formal inter-reviewer agreement (e.g., Cohen's kappa) was not calculated. Reviewers necessarily had access to the clinical record required for diagnosis and temporal classification. Residual reviewer-dependent outcome misclassification remains possible.
Overall event prevalence was 40.29%; training and fixed internal test sets each had approximately 40% events. No synthetic oversampling, undersampling, or SMOTE-type resampling was used.
Stratified split/CV preserved prevalence. RF allowed class_weight=balanced or none; the selected primary RF used none. Other algorithms used standard unweighted objectives.

A 70:30 stratified split was created before preprocessing. Current 11-predictor hyperparameters/calibration were fitted in training; final operating thresholds were derived from strict outer-10-fold cross-fitted calibrated training probabilities with hyperparameters fixed from the full-training Bayesian search.

The fixed test set was previously accessed during iterative revision and is a standardized internal comparison set. Threshold cross-fitting is not a fully nested estimate of the complete development process.
Brier score, calibration intercept and slope, Hosmer-Lemeshow test, ECE, MCE, calibration plots, and bootstrap uncertainty were reported.
Calibration plots used 10 risk groups with 1,000 patient-level bootstrap resamples to obtain 95% pointwise intervals.

HAP-only models used the current 11 predictors and were repeated after removing MV/intubation (9 predictors). Current 11-predictor GBDT/LR probabilities were evaluated across remaining-ICU-stay strata. Models were also refitted in 2020-2023 and tested in 2024-2025 with the current 11-predictor set fixed.

These are post hoc internal robustness analyses. HAP-only addresses VAP/airway overlap; remaining-LOS analyses address observation opportunity descriptively; temporal splitting evaluates calendar-time robustness rather than independent validation.
Reporting was guided by TRIPOD+AI [34]. PROBAST+AI [35] was used only as a framework for discussing methodological limitations; no formal PROBAST+AI risk-of-bias rating was assigned.

Key applicability concerns include single-center sampling, unavailable neurologic/severity variables, variable prediction horizon, outcome ascertainment without standardized microbiology fields, and lack of independent external validation.
Python/R versions, major package versions, random seed, search spaces, selected hyperparameters, thresholds, and revision-specific analyses are documented.
Revision-specific scripts document analysis settings and are available from the corresponding author during peer review; patient-level data will not be included in public code files.
No formal algorithmic-fairness analysis was prespecified.
Future multicenter validation should evaluate discrimination, calibration, and downstream clinical consequences across clinically relevant demographic and clinical subgroups before implementation.

Sequential screening counts are reported in Supplementary Figure S1 and Table S24. The two late-stage exclusion blocks were retained in the revision archive as grouped totals (n=232 and n=311). Within the final included cohort, variables with >30% training-set missingness were excluded and variables with <=30% missingness were imputed using a training-fitted IterativeImputer with a Random Forest estimator, producing a single completed dataset.

Mutually exclusive component counts within the grouped 232- and 311-patient blocks, including the exact number of repeat admissions, were not recoverable from the archived screening log. Excluded-patient covariates were not retained in the analysis-ready dataset, so an included-versus-excluded comparison could not be reconstructed. Multiple imputation was not performed; imputation uncertainty was not propagated.

BSA and the all-zero immunosuppressant field were excluded before current primary selection; cholinesterase-inhibitor exposure was removed by the general training-set zero-variance rule. Thirty-five candidates entered LASSO/Boruta and the intersection retained 11 predictors. Age was then forced into the 11-predictor set to create a 12-predictor sensitivity analysis.

The 11-variable intersection is the current primary set. Boruta confirmed age but LASSO shrank it to zero; forcing age did not consistently improve fixed internal test performance, and no AUC gain remained significant after Holm correction.

Five repeats of stratified 5-fold outer resampling (25 outer folds) reran BSA-free zero-variance screening, LASSO/Boruta feature selection, outer-training scaling, inner 5-fold Bayesian tuning, 5-fold Platt calibration, and cross-fitted training-only Youden-threshold derivation for LR and GBDT before untouched outer-fold evaluation.

The archived input was already imputed and winsorized under the original workflow, so imputation models and winsorization limits could not be re-estimated inside outer folds. The analysis therefore validates the recoverable post-preprocessing pipeline, not the complete raw-data pipeline.

Laboratory predictors used the first available result within 48 hours. Surgery, MV, intubation/tracheotomy, and diuretics were first-48-hour indicators. TCO2 was the first available total carbon dioxide result within 48 hours.

Exact laboratory collection timestamps, procedure-specific surgical details, treatment duration, start/stop times, and active-at-landmark status were not retained in the analysis-ready archive. Thus, the sampling-time distribution and admission-versus-later breakdown cannot be reconstructed, and these predictors are window-level exposure markers.
Focused DCA used the current 11-predictor calibrated test probabilities at thresholds 0.25, 0.30, and 0.40 with 1,000 paired patient-level bootstrap resamples.

The range was introduced post hoc and is not a deployment threshold. Probabilities have a variable horizon to ICU exit; positive net benefit does not establish low resource burden or transportable clinical utility.
Post hoc LR comparators (MV+intubation, NLR, age+sex, and NEU+LYM+MV) were compared with the current 11-predictor LR in the same fixed internal test partition.
The best three-variable comparator remained materially below the 11-predictor LR, supporting algorithmic parsimony but not extreme predictor reduction. The analysis is internal and post hoc.

The binary archive was re-audited for the fields questioned by the reviewer. First-48-hour prevalence was MV 333/3,368 (9.9%), intubation/tracheotomy 353/3,368 (10.5%), CVC 32/3,368 (1.0%), and CRRT 12/3,368 (0.4%). The recorded heart-disease flag was positive in 9 patients; immunosuppressants in 0 and cholinesterase inhibitors in 1. Among 334 VAP cases, 262 lacked a first-48-hour MV indicator and 230 lacked a first-48-hour intubation/tracheotomy indicator. Targeted source-record review was used for VAP subtype re-audit.

Intervention counts are predictor-window exposures rather than full-course unit prevalence. By the VAP definition, VAP cases lacking an early airway indicator received qualifying airway support later in the ICU course, although exact post-landmark start times were not retained in the revision extract. The sparse heart-disease flag is not treated as broad cardiac-comorbidity prevalence or an AF surrogate. The all-zero/one-positive medication fields were a historical candidate-inventory oversight; training zero-variance fields were removed in revision-specific re-selection. A full raw-data re-extraction was not performed.
S17.note: This table is a reporting/transparency summary rather than a participant-level statistical analysis.
